risks.title: Persistent Inflation and Potential Policy Tightening
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated, above central bank targets, leading to concerns about continued monetary policy tightening. This could dampen economic growth and increase borrowing costs.
risks.watch_for: CPI and PCE inflation data, FOMC statements on interest rates.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement / SEP / minutes), July 15, 2026
International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook), July 08, 2026

risks.title: Geopolitical Instability and Commodity Price Volatility
risks.summary: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, are driving up energy prices and threatening supply chains. This volatility can lead to broader economic disruptions and inflationary pressures.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, energy price movements, shipping lane disruptions.
sources: International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook), July 08, 2026
Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes), May 2026

risks.title: Slowing Global Growth Amidst Divergent Economic Performance
risks.summary: Global economic growth is projected to slow, with emerging markets and developing economies facing particularly weak per capita income growth. This divergence is exacerbated by geopolitical events and uneven technological adoption.
risks.watch_for: Global GDP growth forecasts, per capita income growth in EMDEs, trade growth.
sources: International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook), July 08, 2026

risks.title: Persistent Fiscal Deficits and Rising Debt Levels
risks.summary: The US faces significant and growing federal budget deficits and a rising national debt. These trends are driven by increased spending and net interest costs, potentially limiting fiscal flexibility.
risks.watch_for: CBO's Budget and Economic Outlook reports, US national debt figures.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook), February 11, 2026
Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), 2026

risks.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Tariffs
risks.summary: Evolving trade policies and new tariffs continue to impact prices, supply chains, and business investment. While some stimulus measures may offset costs, tariffs can entrench price pressures.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs, trade dispute resolutions, impact on import prices.

risks.title: AI Adoption and its Economic Impact
risks.summary: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence presents both opportunities for productivity growth and potential risks. While AI investment is boosting some sectors, its full economic benefits and potential labor market disruptions are still unfolding.
risks.watch_for: AI investment trends, productivity growth data, labor market impacts of AI.
sources: Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), 2026

risks.title: Labor Market Stabilization Amidst Shifting Dynamics
risks.summary: The labor market shows signs of stabilizing, but concerns remain about job growth and potential shifts due to AI and economic slowdowns. Some forecasts predict a slight rise in unemployment.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate, nonfarm payroll employment, wage growth.
sources: Stanford SIEPR ("US Economy 2026: What to Watch"), 2026
Federal Reserve (FOMC statement / SEP / minutes), June 17, 2026
Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (Survey of Professional Forecasters), May 15, 2026

risks.title: Financial Market Volatility and Policy Uncertainty
risks.summary: Markets are navigating a complex environment with geopolitical tensions, shifting inflation expectations, and potential central bank policy changes. This can lead to increased volatility and uncertainty for investors.
risks.watch_for: Interest rate decisions, bond yields, equity market performance.
sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (Mid-Year Outlook 2026), June 17, 2026

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus that inflation remains a key concern, with several institutions expecting continued elevated levels and potential for further monetary policy tightening. Geopolitical risks, particularly the Middle East conflict, are widely flagged as a significant downside risk, impacting energy prices and global growth. While AI is seen as a driver of growth, its net impact and the potential for labor market disruption are viewed with some caution. Divergence in global growth, with emerging markets lagging, is another prominent theme.
